examples.ko: 지역 문화의 고유성을 지키는 일이 중요해요.
examples.en: Protecting the uniqueness of local culture is important.
Hangeul is a script with outstanding uniqueness.
We made the product while keeping the brand's distinct identity.

examples.ko: 전통 음식의 고유성이 점점 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: The distinctive character of traditional food is gradually disappearing.
When translated, the distinctiveness of this phrase is lost.
Each country has a different kind of uniqueness in its language.

explain: '독창성'은 새롭게 만들어낸 것에 쓰고, '고유성'은 원래부터 그것만이 가진 특징에 써요. '고유성을 지키다', '고유성을 살리다', '고유성을 잃다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 우리는 전통 음식의 고유성을 지키고 싶어요.
phrases.en: We want to protect the uniqueness of traditional food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 가진 특징을 그대로 보호한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means protecting the original character as it is.

phrases.example: 이 건물은 옛 모습의 고유성을 살려서 고쳤어요.
phrases.en: This building was restored while keeping its original character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특징이 잘 보이게 한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like making the distinctive character stand out.

phrases.en: The village lost its uniqueness as it became a tourist spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래의 특징이 사라졌다는 아쉬움을 담아 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said with regret that the original character is gone.

explain_en: '독창성' is for something newly created, while '고유성' is for a trait that something has had all along. Common phrases are '고유성을 지키다', '고유성을 살리다', and '고유성을 잃다'.

examples.en: This car is small, so it is easy to maneuver.
I cut down my luggage to be more mobile.

examples.ko: 기동성 때문에 사람들이 스쿠터를 많이 타요.
examples.en: People ride scooters a lot because of their mobility.
Laptops are portable, but the screen is small.
At the site, safety comes before mobility.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 가벼워서 기동성에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This bag is light, so it helps with getting around.

explain: '기동력'과 비슷해서 서로 바꿔 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 차, 가방, 노트북처럼 가볍고 움직이기 편한 것을 말할 때도 나와요. '기동성이 좋다/떨어지다/높다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: With lots of luggage, your mobility drops.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이기 불편해질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving around becomes harder.

phrases.en: This laptop is light, so it is very portable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 가볍고 들고 다니기 편하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises something light and easy to carry.

phrases.en: Mobility matters for fire trucks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기동성'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with 기동성.

explain_en: It is close to '기동력' and the two are often swapped. It also comes up for things that are light and easy to move, like cars, bags and laptops. People say '기동성이 좋다/떨어지다/높다'.

en: to be astute; to be shrewd

examples.en: He responded quickly and prevented an accident.
Thanks to a quick, sharp judgment, we reduced the loss.
A cat's movements are really nimble.

examples.ko: 저는 행동이 기민하지 않아서 늘 한발 늦어요.
examples.en: I'm not quick to act, so I'm always a step behind.

examples.ko: 점원이 기민했던 덕분에 손님이 오래 기다리지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the clerk's alertness, the customer didn't have to wait long.
In a crisis, you need to be quick and also calm.

explain: 상황을 재빨리 알아채고 알맞게 움직인다는 느낌이에요. '빠르다'는 속도 자체를 말하고, '민첩하다'는 몸놀림이 빠르다는 쪽이 강해요. '기민하다'는 판단과 대처가 빠를 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The firefighters moved swiftly and put out the fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황을 보고 재빨리 알맞게 행동한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means acting quickly and appropriately after reading the situation.

phrases.example: 판단이 기민하지 않으면 좋은 기회를 놓쳐요.
phrases.en: If your judgment isn't quick, you miss good opportunities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 대처가 느리다는 뜻을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says someone's response is slow.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 몸이 민첩해서 공을 잘 잡아요.
phrases.en: That player is agile, so he catches the ball well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기민하다'가 판단과 대처가 빠르다면 '민첩하다'는 몸놀림이 빠르다는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 기민하다 is quick judgment, 민첩하다 leans toward quick body movement.

explain_en: It carries the feel of noticing a situation quickly and acting appropriately. '빠르다' is about speed itself, and '민첩하다' leans toward quick body movement. '기민하다' fits best when judgment and response are fast.

examples.en: It was a presentation that showed the new employee's spirit.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 기백을 잃지 않고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to keep my spirit even as I get older.
A spirited young man stepped forward.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 기백에 눌려서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was overwhelmed by his spirit and couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 기백으로 가득한 응원 소리가 경기장에 울렸어요.
examples.en: Cheers full of spirit rang through the stadium.

examples.ko: 목소리는 작아도 기백만은 누구한테도 지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if my voice is small, I'm second to none in spirit.

explain: '패기'와 비슷하게 굽히지 않는 씩씩한 마음과 태도를 말해요. '기백이 있다/넘치다'처럼 쓰고, 목소리나 표정에서 느껴지는 힘을 칭찬할 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: That young man seems to have spirit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씩씩하고 굽히지 않는 사람에게 쓰는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praise for someone bold who does not back down.

phrases.en: His speech was full of spirit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 아주 많이 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a strong sense of energy is felt.

phrases.en: I envy the boldness of young people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기백'과 비슷하고, 젊은 사람에게 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 기백, used more for young people.

explain_en: Like '패기', it means a bold, unyielding spirit and attitude. People say '기백이 있다/넘치다', and it suits praise for strength felt in a voice or expression.

examples.en: By my own measure, I did my best.

examples.ko: 자기 깜냥도 모르고 큰 일을 맡으려고 해요.
examples.en: He wants to take on a big job without knowing his own limits.

examples.ko: 그 일은 내 깜냥으로는 해결하기 어려워요.
examples.en: That problem is hard to solve with my abilities.

examples.ko: 깜냥이 안 되는 일은 욕심내지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't be greedy about things beyond your capacity.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 깜냥을 넘는 자리에 올라서 힘들어해요.
examples.en: He rose to a position beyond his capacity and is struggling.

examples.ko: 깜냥만큼만 하면 되니까 너무 걱정하지 마요.
examples.en: Just do as much as you can, so don't worry too much.

explain: '능력'은 어디에나 쓰지만 '깜냥'은 '제 깜냥에는', '깜냥이 안 되다'처럼 굳어진 말투로 자주 써요. 한계를 말하거나 겸손하게 말할 때 나오고, '깜냥이 뛰어나다'처럼 칭찬에는 잘 안 써요. 윗사람에게 '제 깜냥에는'이라고 하면 겸손하게 들려요.

phrases.example: 그 일은 제 깜냥이 안 돼서 못 하겠어요.
phrases.en: That job is beyond my ability, so I can't do it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이 부족해서 감당하기 어렵다고 말할 때 써요. 겸손하게 거절할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you lack the ability to handle something. It can also be a modest way to decline.

phrases.example: 처음에는 제 깜냥에 맞는 일부터 시작할게요.
phrases.en: At first I'll start with work that suits my ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 능력에 맞는 정도를 말할 때 써요. '맞는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that matches one's ability. You can use '맞는' to modify a noun.

phrases.example: 자기 깜냥을 알고 무리하지 않는 게 중요해요.
phrases.en: It's important to know your limits and not overreach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 능력의 한계를 안다는 뜻이에요. 충고하는 말에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means knowing the limits of your ability. Often appears in advice.

explain_en: '능력' fits almost any context, but '깜냥' mostly appears in set phrases like '제 깜냥에는' and '깜냥이 안 되다'. It is used to state limits or to sound modest, and rarely for praise, as in '깜냥이 뛰어나다'. Saying '제 깜냥에는' to a superior sounds humble.

en: to be strong; to be firm

examples.ko: 태풍에도 꿋꿋하게 서 있는 나무가 멋있어요.
examples.en: The tree standing firm even in the typhoon looks great.
Grandmother protected the family with her unshaken strength.
He is a resilient child who gets right back up even when he falls.

examples.ko: 친구들은 저를 꿋꿋하다고 하지만 사실 많이 힘들어요.
examples.en: My friends say I am strong, but actually I am having a hard time.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 꿋꿋하니까 걱정 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: That friend is strong, so you don't need to worry.

examples.ko: 늘 꿋꿋하던 형이 오늘은 눈물을 보였어요.
examples.en: My older brother, who was always steady, showed tears today.

explain: '강하다'는 힘이 센 느낌이 있지만, '꿋꿋하다'는 힘든 일 앞에서도 마음이 흔들리지 않는 모습에 써요. '꿋꿋하게 버티다, 살아가다, 견디다'처럼 '-게' 형태로 동사와 잘 어울리고, '꿋꿋이'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I held on firmly even in a hard situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 때 흔들리지 않고 견딘다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means enduring without wavering in hard times.

phrases.en: He firmly walked his own path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿋꿋하게'와 뜻이 같고 부사로 바로 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '꿋꿋하게', used directly as an adverb.

phrases.example: 그녀는 힘든 일 앞에서도 꿋꿋한 태도를 보였어요.
phrases.en: She showed a steadfast attitude even in the face of hardship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들림 없이 굳센 태도나 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an unshaken, steadfast attitude.

explain_en: '강하다' suggests physical strength, but '꿋꿋하다' describes someone whose heart does not waver even in hard times. It pairs well with verbs in the '-게' form, as in '꿋꿋하게 버티다/살아가다/견디다', and you can also say '꿋꿋이'.

en: to be persistent; to be tenacious

examples.en: That person keeps calling persistently.
After persistent effort, I finally passed.
The reporter kept asking questions doggedly.
I laughed at the puppy that kept tagging along.

examples.ko: 그의 끈덕진 성격 덕분에 일이 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to his tenacious character, the work got done.
If you're tenacious, good results will come someday.

explain: 포기하지 않고 끈질기게 계속하는 모습이에요. 비슷한 말로 '끈질기다'가 있고, 상대가 귀찮아할 만큼 계속할 때도 쓸 수 있어요. '끈덕지게'처럼 부사형으로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The detective persistently chased the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끈덕지다'와 비슷하고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '끈덕지다' and used more often.

phrases.en: Reporters keep tailing that actor relentlessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀찮을 만큼 계속 따라다닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone follows so persistently it becomes annoying.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 정말 끈덕져요. 절대 포기하지 않아요.
phrases.en: That friend is really tenacious. He never gives up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form used to describe a person's character.

explain_en: It describes continuing without giving up. A similar word is '끈질기다', and it can also be used when someone keeps going to the point of being annoying. It often appears in the adverb form '끈덕지게'.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 늘 사람이 많고 정말 다이내믹해요.
examples.en: This city always has lots of people and is really dynamic.

examples.ko: 다이내믹한 영상 때문에 눈을 뗄 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't take my eyes off it because of the dynamic footage.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 경기 스타일은 아주 다이내믹했어요.
examples.en: That player's style of play was very dynamic.

examples.ko: 요즘 한국 사회는 너무 다이내믹해서 따라가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Korean society these days is so dynamic that it's hard to keep up.

examples.ko: 좀 더 다이내믹하게 춤을 춰 보세요.
examples.en: Try dancing a bit more dynamically.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 이야기가 다이내믹하지 않아서 조금 지루해요.
examples.en: This drama's story isn't dynamic, so it's a little boring.

explain: '역동적이다'와 비슷하지만 '다이내믹하다'가 더 말하는 느낌이에요. 도시, 경기, 영상, 사회 변화처럼 움직임과 변화가 많은 것에 써요. '역동적'은 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I watched a dynamic game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a following noun.

phrases.en: This movie isn't very dynamic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직임이나 변화가 적다고 말하는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying there is little movement or change.

phrases.en: This city is really dynamic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but more common in news and writing.

explain_en: It is close to '역동적이다', but '다이내믹하다' sounds more like everyday speech. Use it for things with lots of movement and change, such as cities, games, videos and social change. '역동적' appears more often in news and writing.

en: to be clear; to be distinct

examples.en: The child gave the presentation in a clear voice.
Even though she's old, my grandmother's mind is sharp.
That announcer's pronunciation is crisp and clear.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 눈이 또랑또랑해서 믿음이 가요.
examples.en: That student has bright, alert eyes, so I trust him.

examples.ko: 목소리가 또랑또랑하게 들려서 맨 뒤에서도 잘 들렸어요.
examples.en: The voice was so clear that I could hear it even in the very back.

examples.ko: 말투가 또랑또랑하면 면접에서 좋은 인상을 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak clearly, you can make a good impression in an interview.

explain: '또렷하다'는 모양·소리·기억에 두루 쓰고, '또랑또랑하다'는 주로 목소리, 눈빛, 정신이 맑고 야무진 느낌에 써요. 아이나 어르신을 칭찬할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: That child speaks clearly and confidently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목소리가 맑고 야무지게 말하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for speaking in a clear, sharp-sounding voice.

phrases.en: Even though I didn't sleep all night, my eyes are bright and alert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈빛이 맑고 정신이 깨어 있는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes bright eyes and an alert mind.

phrases.en: Even though my grandfather is old, his mind is still sharp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신의 정신이 맑고 야무질 때 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for an elderly person whose mind is clear and sharp.

explain_en: '또렷하다' is used broadly for shapes, sounds and memories, while '또랑또랑하다' is mostly for a voice, eyes or mind that is clear and sharp. It fits well when praising children or older people.

examples.ko: 새로 산 그릇이 매끈매끈해서 닦기 쉬워요.
examples.en: The new bowl is smooth, so it's easy to wash.
After my bath, my skin feels smooth.
I wiped the floor until it was smooth and shiny.
I picked up a smooth stone and put it in my pocket.
When you apply cream, your hands become smooth and soft.

examples.ko: 삶은 달걀 껍데기를 벗기니 속이 매끈매끈했어요.
examples.en: When I peeled the boiled egg, it was smooth inside.

explain: 표면이 걸리는 데 없이 곱고 부드러운 느낌이에요. '미끌미끌'은 미끄러워서 불편하거나 위험한 느낌이 있지만 '매끈매끈'은 보통 좋은 느낌이에요. '매끈하다'도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: This stone feels smooth when I touch it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '매끈매끈'을 형용사로 바꿔 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, used to describe a state of being smooth.

phrases.en: I envy the baby's smooth skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, 피부나 표면이 곱다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for nouns, meaning a fine, smooth surface.

phrases.en: If I put on cream, my hands become smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래와 달리 표면이 부드럽게 변하는 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a surface becoming smooth.

explain_en: It describes a surface that is fine and smooth with nothing catching. '미끌미끌' often feels slippery in an uncomfortable or risky way, while '매끈매끈' usually has a positive feel. Learn '매끈하다' as well.

en: to be complicated; to be intricate; to be complex

examples.en: The world these days is so complex that it's hard to understand.

examples.ko: 이 사건이 일어난 이유는 아주 복잡다단해요.
examples.en: The reasons this incident happened are very complicated.
Many tangled emotions came rushing in all at once.

examples.ko: 현대 사회의 문제는 복잡다단하기 때문에 한 가지 답이 없어요.
examples.en: Because problems in modern society are so intricate, there is no single answer.

examples.ko: 그 두 나라의 관계는 복잡다단하게 얽혀 있어요.
examples.en: The relationship between those two countries is intricately entangled.
I gave up applying because of the complicated procedure.

explain: '복잡하다'보다 격식 있는 말로, 일이나 사정이 여러 갈래로 얽혀 있다는 느낌이에요. 사람이 붐비는 곳에는 쓰지 않고 상황, 감정, 관계에 써요. 말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: It's a complex problem, so it needs time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 명사를 꾸며요. 여러 갈래로 얽힌 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form modifies a noun, used for tangled, multi-layered matters.

phrases.en: The relationship between the two countries is intricate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 모양이에요. 관계나 상황이 얽혀 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, used when relations or situations are tangled.

phrases.en: My head is so cluttered these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 사람이 붐비는 곳에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more common word; it can also describe crowded places.

explain_en: It is more formal than '복잡하다' and suggests matters or circumstances tangled in many directions. It is used for situations, feelings and relationships, not for crowded places. It appears more in writing and news than in speech.

examples.en: Ripe strawberries are bright red.

examples.ko: 선홍색 립스틱을 바르니 얼굴이 환해 보여요.
examples.en: With bright red lipstick on, my face looks brighter.
Fresh tuna is a bright red color.
The evening sky was tinted bright red.
I went to the party wearing a bright red dress.
The petals gradually changed from bright red to light pink.

explain: 선명하고 밝은 붉은색이에요. 그냥 '빨간색'보다 맑고 생생한 느낌이라서, 신선한 고기·생선이나 꽃, 노을의 색을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The sky was dyed bright red.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선홍색'과 거의 같지만 '빛'이라서 번지는 빛깔의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 선홍색, but 빛 gives a feeling of a spreading glow of color.

phrases.en: Bright red petals fluttered in the spring wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃처럼 선명한 붉은 것을 설명할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It fits vivid red things such as flowers.

phrases.en: Fresh meat is bright red.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 맑고 싱싱하다는 뜻을 함께 전해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It also conveys that the color looks clear and fresh.

explain_en: It is a clear, bright red. It feels fresher and more vivid than plain '빨간색', so it suits the color of fresh meat and fish, flowers and sunsets.

examples.en: This outfit is simple, but you can feel its sophistication.
That café stands out for the refinement of its interior.
It has a sophisticated design, so it's very popular.
If you cut down on colors, the elegance actually comes through.
Refinement shows in the way she speaks.

examples.ko: 가구 배치만 바꿔도 방에 세련미를 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Just rearranging the furniture can give the room a touch of sophistication.

explain: '세련되다'가 상태라면 '세련미'는 그 안에서 느껴지는 멋을 말해서 '세련미가 느껴지다', '세련미가 돋보이다'처럼 자주 써요. 옷, 디자인, 말투, 공간에 두루 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I can feel the sophistication in this bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 분위기에서 멋이 자연스럽게 전해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sense of style comes through naturally in the look or atmosphere.

phrases.en: The sophistication stands out in the simple design.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 것보다 세련된 멋이 눈에 띌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the refined style stands out more than other things.

phrases.en: It is a design full of sophistication.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세련된 멋이 아주 많이 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a strong sense of refined style comes through.

explain_en: If '세련되다' describes a state, '세련미' is the stylish quality you feel in it, so you often hear '세련미가 느껴지다' and '세련미가 돋보이다'. It works for clothes, design, speech and spaces.

examples.en: Social media clearly has good functions too.

examples.ko: 적당한 경쟁은 성장을 돕는 순기능이 있어요.
examples.en: Moderate competition has a positive function in helping growth.
I read a paper that studied the positive effects of games.
Many rules are inconvenient, but their benefits are clear too.

examples.ko: 인터넷의 순기능만 보지 말고 부작용도 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't look only at the good side of the internet; think about the side effects too.
We need to look at both the positive and negative functions.

explain: 어떤 제도나 기술이 사회에 주는 좋은 작용을 말해요. 반대말은 '역기능'이고, 보통 'N의 순기능'과 'N의 역기능'을 짝으로 이야기해요.

phrases.en: Games also have a positive function.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것이 사회에 주는 좋은 작용이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something has a good effect on society.

phrases.en: We talked about the good and bad functions of the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '역기능'과 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with its opposite, '역기능'.

phrases.en: This system has a big positive effect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 작용이 크다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the good effect is large.

explain_en: It refers to the good effect that a system or technology has on society. The opposite is '역기능', and people usually discuss 'N의 순기능' and 'N의 역기능' as a pair.

examples.en: This idea is really neat, isn't it?
You look much fresher after the haircut.

examples.ko: 일 처리를 쌈박하게 해 줘서 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you for handling the work so neatly.
The design was so sleek that I bought it right away.

examples.ko: 새 가게에 어울리는 쌈박한 이름이 없을까요?
examples.en: Isn't there a snappy name that suits the new shop?
I feel good because I wrapped up the presentation cleanly.

explain: 말끔하고 산뜻해서 마음에 들 때 칭찬하는 말이에요. 아이디어, 디자인, 일 처리처럼 깔끔하고 시원한 것에 써요. 글보다 말에서 편하게 쓰는 구어예요.

phrases.en: A neat idea came to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깔끔하고 시원한 생각을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises an idea that is clean and clever.

phrases.en: I finished the work neatly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 말끔하게 처리했다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a task was wrapped up cleanly.

phrases.en: The room is tidy, so I like it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌈박하다'보다 더 널리 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more widely used, similar word.

explain_en: It is a compliment for something clean, fresh and satisfying. It fits ideas, designs and the way a job is handled when they feel neat and crisp. It is more of a spoken word than a written one.

examples.ko: 이 개는 아직 야성이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: This dog still has some wildness left in it.

examples.ko: 사자는 우리에서 자라도 야성을 잃지 않아요.
examples.en: Lions don't lose their wild nature even if raised in a cage.
That player is famous for his raw, wild style of play.

examples.ko: 아이들은 자연 속에서 야성을 되찾는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Kids seem to get their wild side back in nature.
The eyes full of wildness are impressive.
An actor with a lot of rugged charm is popular these days.

explain: '야생'은 자연에서 사는 상태를 말하고, '야성'은 길들여지지 않은 거친 본성이나 성질을 말해요. 동물뿐 아니라 사람에게도 써서 '야성적이다', '야성미'처럼 말해요. 거칠지만 힘 있고 매력적인 느낌으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: That actor has a wild charm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 거칠지만 힘 있는 매력이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people, it means a rough but powerful kind of charm.

phrases.en: The look full of wild charm is really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거친 매력을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a rugged kind of attractiveness.

phrases.example: 풀어 준 새가 금방 야성을 되찾았어요.
phrases.en: The released bird quickly regained its wild nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길들여졌던 동물이 본래 성질로 돌아갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tamed animal returns to its natural instincts.

explain_en: '야생' means living in the wild, while '야성' means an untamed, rough nature or quality. It can describe people as well as animals, as in '야성적이다' and '야성미'. It is often used with a rough but powerful, attractive feel.

en: to be courageous; to be brave

examples.en: The valiant general led the way and blocked the enemy.

examples.ko: 사자는 용맹하고 당당한 동물로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: The lion is known as a brave and dignified animal.
That soldier fought bravely and got hurt.

examples.ko: 용맹해 보이는 호랑이 그림이 벽에 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A painting of a fierce-looking tiger hangs on the wall.
The child smiled after being praised as brave.
A person who is brave but not careful is dangerous.

explain: '용감하다'보다 글 느낌이 강하고, 싸움에서 힘 있게 맞서는 모습에 어울려요. 사람, 동물, 군대에 써요. '용맹스럽다'라고도 하지만 쓰임은 거의 같아요. 일상 대화에서는 '용감하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Brave soldiers protected the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 군대를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used for people or armies.

phrases.en: Tigers are really fierce and brave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 문장을 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for ending a sentence.

phrases.en: Firefighters are really brave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용맹하다보다 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Far more common in daily life than 용맹하다.

explain_en: It sounds more literary than '용감하다' and suits someone facing a fight with strength. It is used for people, animals and armies. '용맹스럽다' also exists with almost the same use. In daily talk '용감하다' is far more common.

en: to be skilled; to be experienced; to be masterful

examples.en: That actor's performances get more mature as time goes on.
With masterful skill, he finished the dish in no time.
As I got older, my way of thinking became more mature.
The way she solved the problem with such mastery was impressive.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 원숙하지 않아서 실수가 많아요.
examples.en: I'm not yet seasoned, so I make a lot of mistakes.

examples.ko: 경력이 길어서 그런지 일 처리가 원숙해 보여요.
examples.en: Maybe because of your long career, the way you handle work looks seasoned.

explain: 오랜 경험으로 기술이나 인격, 연기가 무르익어 안정된 상태를 말해요. '능숙하다'는 손에 익어 잘한다는 뜻이 강하고, '원숙하다'는 깊이와 여유까지 느껴져요. 보통 칭찬할 때 써요.

phrases.en: That actor is loved for his seasoned acting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형으로, 연기나 솜씨를 칭찬할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, often used to praise acting or skill.

phrases.en: Your skill becomes more mature as you get older.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 지나면서 점점 무르익는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gradual ripening of skill over time.

phrases.en: My teacher's piano playing is truly masterful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 오랜 경험으로 무르익은 실력을 칭찬하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite sentence-ending form praising skill ripened through long experience.

explain_en: It describes skill, character or acting that has ripened and steadied through long experience. '능숙하다' mainly means being practiced and good at something, while 원숙하다 also suggests depth and composure. It is usually used as praise.

examples.ko: 이 차는 유선형이라서 바람 소리가 적어요.
examples.en: This car is streamlined, so there's little wind noise.

examples.ko: 돌고래의 몸은 물속에서 빠르게 움직이는 유선형이에요.
examples.en: A dolphin's body is streamlined so it can move fast in water.
A streamlined train pulled into the station.

examples.ko: 수영할 때 몸을 유선형으로 만들면 더 빨라요.
examples.en: When you swim, you go faster if you make your body streamlined.
Most airplanes have a shape close to streamlined.
The bottle has a smooth curved shape, so it's comfortable to hold.

explain: 자동차, 기차, 비행기, 물고기처럼 빨리 움직이는 것의 모양을 말할 때 써요. '유선형 디자인', '유선형으로 만들다'처럼 쓰고, 일상에서는 '매끈한 모양'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 자전거는 유선형 디자인이라서 빨라 보여요.
phrases.en: This bike has a streamlined design, so it looks fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 소개할 때 자주 붙여 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for describing the shape of a product.

phrases.example: 배를 유선형으로 만들면 물의 저항이 줄어요.
phrases.en: If you make a ship streamlined, water resistance goes down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 어떻게 만드는지 말할 때 '-으로 만들다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-으로 만들다' to say how something is shaped.

phrases.example: 이 차는 모양이 매끈해서 눈에 띄어요.
phrases.en: This car has a sleek shape, so it stands out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유선형' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say '유선형'.

explain_en: It describes the shape of things that move fast, such as cars, trains, planes and fish. It appears in phrases like '유선형 디자인' and '유선형으로 만들다', and in daily talk people also say '매끈한 모양' (a smooth shape).

en: to be docile; to be gentle; to be mild

examples.ko: 이 강아지는 성격이 유순해서 아이들도 좋아해요.
examples.en: This puppy has a gentle nature, so even children like it.
His words are rough, but his heart is gentle.

examples.ko: 유순한 말투 덕분에 사람들이 편하게 이야기해요.
examples.en: Thanks to her gentle way of speaking, people talk to her comfortably.
Cows behave gently, unlike how they look.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 유순했는데 요즘은 고집이 세졌어요.
examples.en: He was docile as a child, but lately he has become stubborn.
That friend who used to be so mild got angry.

explain: 사람이나 동물의 성격이 부드럽고 말을 잘 들을 때 써요. '순하다'가 더 편한 말이고 '유순하다'는 글이나 설명에서 자주 보여요. 반대말은 '사납다', '거칠다'예요.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 유순한 성격이라서 화를 잘 안 내요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling has a gentle personality and rarely gets angry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유순하다'를 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로, 성격을 소개할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun, common when describing personality.

phrases.en: That cat isn't very docile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 말하면 부드럽지 않고 말을 잘 안 듣는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means it isn't gentle and doesn't obey easily.

phrases.example: 이 소는 아주 순해서 아이들이 만져도 괜찮아요.
phrases.en: This cow is very gentle, so it's fine for kids to touch it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유순하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual everyday word than '유순하다'.

explain_en: It describes a person or animal with a soft nature that does what it is told. '순하다' is the plainer everyday word, while '유순하다' shows up more in writing and explanations. Its opposites are '사납다' and '거칠다'.

examples.en: Our team is really cohesive.
We had a meal together to build more unity.
Cohesion doesn't appear overnight.
Their teamwork is good and their cohesion is impressive too.
The cohesive team won the championship in the end.

examples.ko: 그 동네는 주민들의 응집력으로 위기를 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: That neighborhood overcame the crisis thanks to its residents' unity.

explain: 사람들이 한마음으로 뭉치는 힘을 말하고, '응집력이 강하다/높다/약하다/떨어지다'처럼 써요. '단결력'과 비슷하지만 모임이나 팀이 얼마나 끈끈한지 그 상태를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 과학 시간에는 물질의 입자가 서로 뭉치는 힘을 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 동아리는 응집력이 강해서 일을 빨리 끝내요.
phrases.en: This club has strong cohesion, so it finishes work quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이 얼마나 끈끈한지 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for how tightly a group is bound.

phrases.example: 회식은 팀의 응집력을 높이는 데 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: Team dinners help raise the team's cohesion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단결이 더 잘 되도록 만든다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the group more united.

phrases.en: As conflict arose, the team's cohesion dropped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 서로 흩어지고 단결이 약해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people drift apart and unity weakens.

explain_en: It means the force that holds people together as one, used like '응집력이 강하다/높다/약하다/떨어지다'. It is close to '단결력' but fits best when describing how tight-knit a group or team is. In science class it can also mean the force that holds particles of a substance together.

en: to be resolute; to be firm; to be unwavering

examples.ko: 그는 큰 병 앞에서도 의연하게 행동했어요.
examples.en: He acted composedly even in the face of a serious illness.
His steady manner put everyone at ease.
My mother stayed strong even in her sorrow.
The way you handle it calmly is admirable.

examples.ko: 비난에도 의연할 수 있는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a person who can stay firm even under criticism.
I tried to look composed, but my hands were shaking.

explain: 어려운 일이나 슬픔 앞에서도 흔들리지 않고 침착한 태도를 말해요. 사람의 태도를 좋게 말할 때 써요. '의젓하다'와 비슷하지만 '의연하다'는 위기나 슬픔 속의 태도에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Everyone was moved by his composed attitude.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 상황에서도 흔들리지 않는 태도를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise an unshaken attitude in hard times.

phrases.example: 그녀는 슬픈 일을 겪고도 의연해 보였어요.
phrases.en: She looked composed even after a sad event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 침착해 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone looks calm and steady on the outside.

phrases.en: The players dealt with the crisis calmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 생겼을 때 침착하게 대하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes handling a problem calmly.

explain_en: It describes staying steady and calm in the face of hardship or sorrow, and is used as praise for a person's attitude. It is similar to '의젓하다', but '의연하다' fits better for one's attitude in a crisis or in grief.

examples.en: He has such fine character that everyone respects him.
A person's character shows in small actions.
I want to be like my teacher in character.

examples.ko: 인품 좋은 사장님 밑에서 일해서 행복해요.
examples.en: I'm happy working under a boss with a good character.

examples.ko: 실력도 중요하지만 인품만 보고 뽑기도 해요.
examples.en: Skill matters, but sometimes they hire based on character alone.

examples.ko: 인품도 갖춘 사람이 리더가 되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope someone with good character as well becomes the leader.

explain: 성격 중에서도 사람됨과 품위를 평가하는 말이라 '인품이 좋다/훌륭하다/높다'처럼 좋은 쪽에 써요. 그냥 성격을 말할 때는 '성격'이 더 자연스러워요. 존경하는 어른이나 윗사람 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The teacher has excellent character, so students follow him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존경하는 어른이나 윗사람에게 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation that suits respected elders or superiors.

phrases.en: A leader must have both skill and good character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람됨과 품위를 모두 가졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means having good character and dignity.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 성격이 좋아서 인기가 많아요.
phrases.en: My friend has a good personality, so he's popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그냥 성격을 말할 때는 '인품'보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For general personality, this sounds more natural than 인품.

explain_en: It evaluates a person's character and dignity, so it is used on the positive side, as in '인품이 좋다/훌륭하다/높다'. For plain personality, '성격' sounds more natural. It fits talk about respected elders or superiors.

examples.en: Above all, honesty is the most important thing for a politician.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 직원의 정직성을 가장 먼저 봐요.
examples.en: This company looks at an employee's integrity first.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 정직성은 누구도 의심하지 않아요.
examples.en: Nobody doubts that person's honesty.

examples.ko: 면접관이 정직성에 관한 질문을 자주 해요.
examples.en: Interviewers often ask questions about honesty.

examples.ko: 정직성 때문에 친구들이 그를 믿고 비밀을 말해요.
examples.en: Because of his honesty, his friends trust him and tell him their secrets.

examples.ko: 작은 거짓말 하나가 정직성까지 의심하게 만들어요.
examples.en: One small lie makes people doubt even your honesty.

explain: '정직'과 거의 같지만 '정직성'은 사람이나 조직이 가진 성질로 보고 평가하거나 따질 때 써요. '정직성이 높다', '정직성을 의심하다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '정직한 사람이에요'처럼 형용사로 말해도 돼요.

phrases.en: This employee has a high level of honesty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성질을 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when evaluating a person's character.

phrases.en: People doubt his honesty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿지 못하겠다는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when expressing distrust.

phrases.en: I want to work with an honest person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 이렇게 형용사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, people use this adjective form.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '정직' (honesty), but '정직성' treats honesty as a quality of a person or organization that you evaluate or question. You say '정직성이 높다' or '정직성을 의심하다'. In daily talk you can also just say '정직한 사람이에요' with the adjective.

examples.en: I like this fabric because its texture is soft.
The painter expressed a rough texture with paint.
The chewy texture of the bread is really good.
You can't feel the texture well in a photo.

examples.ko: 벽지 질감 때문에 방이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: The room looks warm because of the wallpaper texture.

examples.ko: 손으로 만져 보면 질감을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell the texture by touching it with your hand.

explain: 질감은 손으로 만지거나 눈으로 봤을 때 느껴지는 표면의 느낌이에요. 음식에서는 보통 '식감'이라고 하고, 옷이나 그림, 화장품에서는 질감을 써요. '부드러운 질감', '거친 질감'처럼 형용사와 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: This wallpaper has a unique texture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 것과 다른 표면의 느낌을 말할 때 형용사와 같이 써요. 음식에는 '식감'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with an adjective to describe a surface feel unlike others. For food, 식감 is used instead.

phrases.example: 이 크림은 질감이 좋아서 잘 발라져요.
phrases.en: This cream has a nice texture, so it spreads well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만지거나 발랐을 때 느낌이 마음에 든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you like how it feels when touched or applied.

phrases.en: I brought out the texture of the fabric in the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림이나 사진에서 표면의 느낌이 잘 보이게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the surface feel come through well in a picture or photo.

explain_en: 질감 is the feeling of a surface, whether touched or seen. For food, Koreans usually say 식감 instead, and use 질감 for clothes, paintings, and cosmetics. It pairs with adjectives, as in 부드러운 질감 and 거친 질감.

en: to be innocent; to be guiltless

examples.en: The child is smiling innocently.
Everyone smiled at the child's innocent expression.
That child is cute because of the innocent way he talks.
He is really innocent for his age.
The way he played with the puppy was truly innocent.

examples.ko: 아이들은 천진스럽지만 때로는 너무 솔직해서 놀라요.
examples.en: Kids are innocent, but sometimes so frank that I'm startled.

explain: 꾸밈없이 순수하고 어린아이 같은 모습에 써요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '천진스러워요'가 되고, '천진난만하다'와 함께 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The baby's innocent smile is so pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun.

phrases.en: The way the children play is innocent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ 불규칙' 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form of the ㅂ-irregular.

phrases.en: That child smiles innocently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning and heard more often.

explain_en: It describes a natural, pure, childlike manner. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '천진스러워요', and it is often heard alongside '천진난만하다'.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 청순한 이미지로 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That actress is popular for her pure, innocent image.

examples.ko: 하얀 원피스를 입으니 정말 청순해 보여요.
examples.en: In a white dress, you look really pure and fresh.
Her fresh, innocent smile was captured in the photo.
She is a singer with a clear, pure voice.
They say she has looked innocent and fresh since childhood.
She looks innocent but also handles strong roles well.

explain: 꾸미지 않아도 맑고 깨끗한 인상을 말할 때 쓰고, 주로 여성의 외모나 이미지에 자주 써요. '순수하다'는 마음에 많이 쓰고, 청순하다는 겉모습에서 받는 느낌에 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 청순한 얼굴이라서 인기가 많아요.
phrases.en: That singer is popular because of her innocent, pure-looking face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '청순한 이미지'처럼 외모에서 받는 맑은 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the clean, fresh impression given by someone's looks, like 'a pure image'.

phrases.en: You look even more innocent with your hair down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기본형을 해요체로 말한 것으로, 눈앞의 모습을 바로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요-form, used to comment directly on how someone looks right now.

phrases.en: This makeup gives a pure, fresh feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느낌을 주다'와 함께 스타일이나 화장이 주는 인상을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 느낌을 주다 to talk about the impression a style or makeup gives.

explain_en: It describes a clear, clean impression that needs no makeup, and is often used for a woman's looks or image. '순수하다' is used more for the heart, while 청순하다 is more for the impression given by appearance.

en: to be outstanding; to be prominent

examples.ko: 그 선수는 실력이 출중해서 팀의 에이스예요.
examples.en: That player's skills are outstanding, so he is the team's ace.
He is a person with outstanding looks and a good personality.
Thanks to his outstanding ability, he was promoted early.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 특별히 출중하지는 않지만 성실해요.
examples.en: That student isn't especially outstanding, but he is diligent.

examples.ko: 그녀는 어릴 때부터 그림 실력이 출중했어요.
examples.en: Since she was little, her drawing skills have been outstanding.
A new employee who looks exceptional has joined.

explain: '뛰어나다'보다 격식 있고 글에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 사람의 재능, 실력, 외모처럼 여럿 중에서 눈에 띄게 훌륭한 점에 쓰고, 물건에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: That chef is famous for outstanding skill.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출중한'은 뒤에 명사가 와서 실력이나 재능을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '출중한' form comes before a noun to praise skill or talent.

phrases.en: That child's singing skill is outstanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출중하다'의 해요체예요. '솜씨가', '실력이'처럼 능력을 나타내는 말과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요 form. It goes well with words for ability, such as '솜씨가' or '실력이'.

phrases.en: That player's skill is really excellent.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출중하다'보다 덜 격식적이고 말할 때 훨씬 자주 써요. 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than '출중하다' and much more common in speech. It can also be used for things.

explain_en: It is more formal than '뛰어나다' (to be excellent) and common in writing. It is used for a person's talent, skill or looks that stand out among many, and is rarely used for objects.

en: to be crude; to be coarse

examples.ko: 이 그릇은 모양이 투박스럽지만 정이 가요.
examples.en: This bowl looks crude, but I'm fond of it.

examples.ko: 그는 말투가 투박스러워서 처음에는 무서워 보였어요.
examples.en: His way of speaking was rough, so he seemed scary at first.

examples.ko: 투박스러운 손으로 정성껏 김치를 담가 주셨어요.
examples.en: With her rough hands, she carefully made kimchi for us.
It's a clunky-looking bag, but it's very sturdy.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 표현이 투박스러워도 마음은 따뜻해요.
examples.en: Even though he expresses himself roughly, he has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 투박스러워 보이던 옷이 입어 보니 편했어요.
examples.en: The clothes that looked coarse were comfortable once I tried them on.

explain: '투박하다'로도 같은 뜻을 말해요. 거칠고 세련되지 않았다는 뜻이지만, 소박하고 정이 간다는 긍정적인 느낌으로 쓰기도 해요. 물건, 말투, 손, 사람에게 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: This cup is a bit crude, but it's sturdy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '투박스럽다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 더 짧게 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 투박스럽다, and used more often because it's shorter.

phrases.en: My grandfather's rough hands were warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거칠지만 정이 느껴지는 사람의 손을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits describing rough hands that still feel warm and kind.

phrases.en: This bag isn't clunky; it's pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세련되고 깔끔하다고 말하고 싶을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used to say something looks refined and neat.

explain_en: The same meaning can also be expressed with '투박하다'. It means rough and unrefined, but it can carry a positive feel of being plain and endearing. It can describe objects, speech, hands and people.
